# Hold newborn film windows for the measured dialogue

## Context

Sub of #15252, the continuous flagship film. The tear-out-first screenplay is merged through `#19097` / PR `#19107` at `e6b7b10556ce4e8cbe4a757e35b013c02f52ae9e`. Dialogue draft 2 is [recorded on the parent](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15252#issuecomment-5792910225); voices are Emmy/marin and Mnemosyne/nova, using the recovered July production pipeline.

The first timing rehearsal generated 23 immutable utterance WAVs. Measurements: the mid-birth Emmy line is **4.000 s**, the following Mnemosyne question **2.350 s**, and the re-entry invitation **2.800 s**. The full audio-only listening preview is 67.500 s with declared turn gaps; that is not a finished film duration or visual acceptance receipt.

## The Problem

`NativeGestureDriver.executeTearOutStep` has no stationary post-birth hold. After the real birth gate, it performs the survival moves and immediately re-enters or releases. The narration can therefore describe a window and a held pointer after that visual state has already ended.

Changing the cue's `pause.ms` does not solve this: `TourRunner` starts the cue and pause concurrently, then awaits host settlement. `targetSeconds` is a screenplay budget, not a runtime timer. Slowing the entire pointer path would conflate a deliberate visual hold with gesture motion.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/workstation/tour/NativeGestureDriver.mjs#executeTearOutStep` owns the witnessed pointer bracket and native birth/re-entry/release phases.
- `GestureDriver.runGesture` retains dispatched-input cleanup, and `driver.trap(driver.timeout(...))` is already the cancellable pacing idiom used by the preview dwell.
- `apps/workstation/tour/fiveBeatFilm.mjs` owns app-specific cue options; stable scene/cue IDs bind the separate dialogue assets.
- Existing cue-free `pause` steps can hold a settled result. A new narration engine or runner vocabulary is unnecessary.
- `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/GestureDriver.spec.mjs` owns driver lifecycle/cleanup controls; the existing film whitebox witness owns the continuous real journey.

## The Fix

Add an optional, default-zero `birthDwellMs` to the existing tear-out executor. Place it after confirmed birth/survival and before re-entry or terminal release. Keep the pointer down without synthesizing movement during the hold. Use the existing registered timeout/trap and cleanup path so cancellation/destruction cannot leave input pressed.

Use the measured dialogue map to set the film's hold and ordinary post-receipt pauses. Preserve the opening's short introduction and all existing scene/cue IDs. Correct the cold-open wording or timing against its measured duration before calling the combined rehearsal ready; the current eight-word line measures 4.650 s against a ≤3 s target.

| New `executeTearOutStep` option `birthDwellMs` | existing native gesture executor | a positive duration holds the already-born vessel with pointer down before re-entry/release | omitted/zero preserves existing timing; destruction cancels wait and releases input through existing cleanup | method JSDoc | phase-order and destroy-during-hold controls |
| Film cue pacing | existing `fiveBeatFilmScript` | hold durations come from actual utterance measurements; settled-result holds use pause-only steps | optional commentary may be shortened/omitted, never invent a visual outcome | screenplay header + parent timing receipt | exact-head continuous replay; unchanged cue identities |
| Dialogue assets | parent dialogue draft and recorded voice decisions | immutable WAVs, measured durations, hashes and cue bindings in private production artifacts | changed line creates a successor attempt | parent public receipt, existing owner record | decode/format/content checks; final perceptual/picture QA stays with the take |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The default-zero path preserves the existing tear-out/morph behavior.
- [ ] With a positive hold, no re-entry move or terminal pointer-up occurs until the hold settles; birth still precedes the hold.
- [ ] Destroying/cancelling during the hold settles the run and releases input without late scripted moves.
- [ ] The film uses the measured hold without changing scene/cue IDs or weakening ownership/painted-liveness assertions.
- [ ] A focused real film replay remains green; native display capture and whole-media acceptance stay explicitly on #15252.
- [ ] The parent receives a hash-bound dialogue/timing rehearsal receipt with cold-open duration and mid-gesture timing limits stated.

## Out of Scope

Final video capture/publication; whole-film acceptance; new runtime audio playback or a generalized narration runner; the independent renderer issue `#19110`; unrelated-root isolation `#19103`.

## Avoided Traps

A longer cue-bearing pause does not create a mid-gesture hold. Poll-attempt ceilings are not pacing. A successful audio decode is not a full perceptual listen or a picture-sync proof. Keep old attempts immutable and reuse the July pipeline.

none — app-owned choreography pacing on existing gesture/lifecycle primitives.
